AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we sprinkle soil or old compost between layers? (1 mark)
   A. It adds plastic
   B. It keeps birds away
   C. It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   D. It makes the heap sweeter

2. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Only near the bucket
   B. Next to each plant
   C. Far away from the plants
   D. Only at the end of the row

3. Why is a cloth placed over the opening of the water container? (1 mark)
   A. To make the container heavier
   B. To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   C. To colour the water
   D. To make the water hot

4. Why should the drip container be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To warm the water
   B. To increase evaporation
   C. To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   D. To make water sweet

5. Which is a benefit of using less fuel? (1 mark)
   A. The family saves money
   B. More trees must be cut
   C. More smoke is made
   D. The family spends more

6. Which action wastes fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Using dry wood
   B. Turning the flame down after boiling starts
   C. Using a lid
   D. Boiling water with no lid and a big flame

7. What is a good first step if a person's clothes catch fire? (1 mark)
   A. Run fast
   B. Jump in the air
   C. Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   D. Wave the arms

8. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It creates rain
   B. It makes the room too cold
   C. It gives off a poisonous gas
   D. It makes the walls bigger

9. Which person is protecting wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. A hunter who sets a trap
   B. A person who burns a forest
   C. A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   D. A person who poisons birds

10. Which part holds the head of the scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. The top of the pole
   B. The tin
   C. The dry grass on the ground
   D. The fence

11. Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Wet leaves
   B. Mud
   C. Soil
   D. Old CDs or shiny strips

12. What is direct sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Watering seeds
   B. Sowing in a nursery
   C. Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   D. Buying young plants

13. Why should a seedbed for tiny seeds be fine? (1 mark)
   A. Fine soil makes seeds bigger
   B. It is a school rule
   C. Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   D. Lumps help seeds

14. Which nutrient do oranges and guavas supply in large amounts? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Vitamin C
   C. Starch
   D. Salt

15. Which sign shows a purple passion fruit is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. A white flower
   B. Bright green skin
   C. Hard green skin
   D. Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle

16. What is the main job of the trunk of a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Make flowers
   B. Absorb sunlight
   C. Collect rain
   D. Carry water and food between roots and leaves

17. Why do we weed around fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Weeds protect the stem
   B. Weeds give fruits
   C. Weeds take water and food from the plants
   D. Weeds add sugar

18. How far apart may passion fruit plants be planted? (1 mark)
   A. Touching
   B. About 2 to 3 metres
   C. 30 metres
   D. 10 cm

19. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Cow
   B. Goat
   C. Hen
   D. Dog

20. What does variety mean in eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating one food only
   B. Eating many different kinds of food
   C. Eating a lot
   D. Eating slowly

21. What is shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Baking in an oven
   B. Cooking in a lot of deep oil
   C. Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   D. Cooking in water

22. Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan? (1 mark)
   A. A ladle only
   B. A spatula
   C. A sieve
   D. A bucket

23. What should you do after coughing into your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Shake hands
   B. Wipe them on your clothes
   C. Ignore it
   D. Wash your hands with soap and water

24. Which part is often forgotten when washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. The elbows only
   B. Under the nails and between the fingers
   C. The knees
   D. Only the palms

25. Why do we sweep before mopping? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To use more soap
   C. Because mops cannot touch water
   D. To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud

26. Which of these is an improvised duster? (1 mark)
   A. A stone
   B. A bottle
   C. A tin
   D. A piece of clean old cloth

27. Which is recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Sending it to sea
   B. Burying it
   C. Turning used material into something new
   D. Burning it

28. What should you never do with a needle? (1 mark)
   A. Use a thimble
   B. Thread it
   C. Put it in your mouth
   D. Keep it in a pin cushion

29. What should you do with tacking when permanent sewing is done? (1 mark)
   A. Wash it
   B. Cut and pull it out
   C. Leave it for ever
   D. Dye it

30. What size square did we cut for the handkerchief? (1 mark)
   A. 2 cm by 2 cm
   B. 25 cm by 25 cm
   C. 1 m by 1 m
   D. 5 m by 5 m

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name two materials that can be used to make compost. (2 marks)

32. State the functions of roots, leaves and flowers in a fruit tree. (3 marks)

33. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

34. Describe how to make even tacking. (4 marks)

35. Explain how mulch and compost help a young fruit tree. (4 marks)

36. Explain why a tippy tap is useful in a school without a tap. (3 marks)

37. Explain the meaning of domestic hygiene. (2 marks)

38. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

39. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)

40. Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel. (3 marks)

41. Name two other ways of saving water in the garden. (2 marks)

42. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

43. State three safety rules when cleaning PPE. (3 marks)

44. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

45. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

46. What should be done with a paper dust mask that is dirty? (2 marks)

47. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   Soil and old compost carry bacteria and fungi that break down wastes.

2. B — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

3. B — To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   Dirt would clog the tiny holes.

4. C — To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   A cover keeps water clean and stops mosquitoes breeding.

5. A — The family saves money
   Buying less fuel means spending less.

6. D — Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   Heat escapes without a lid and a big flame.

7. C — Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   Rolling smothers the flames.

8. C — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

9. C — A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   Reporting poaching helps protect animals.

10. A — The top of the pole
   The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

11. D — Old CDs or shiny strips
   Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

12. C — Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   The seedlings are never moved.

13. C — Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   Tiny seeds have little food and are weak.

14. B — Vitamin C
   Citrus fruits and guavas are rich in vitamin C.

15. D — Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   Purple types change colour when ripe.

16. D — Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   The trunk is like a pipe for the plant.

17. C — Weeds take water and food from the plants
   Weeds compete with the crop.

18. B — About 2 to 3 metres
   Give climbers room.

19. D — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

20. B — Eating many different kinds of food
   Variety means different foods.

21. C — Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer of oil.

22. B — A spatula
   A spatula lifts and turns food.

23. D — Wash your hands with soap and water
   Germs from coughs stay on hands.

24. B — Under the nails and between the fingers
   Germs hide there.

25. D — To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud
   Mopping dirt makes mud.

26. D — A piece of clean old cloth
   Old cloth makes a duster.

27. C — Turning used material into something new
   Recycling reuses materials.

28. C — Put it in your mouth
   Needles are dangerous in the mouth.

29. B — Cut and pull it out
   Tacking is temporary.

30. B — 25 cm by 25 cm
   A small handkerchief is easy to make.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the tree and take in water; leaves make food using sunlight; flowers form fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; bring the needle up; make 1 cm stitches with 1 cm gaps along the line; keep the thread loose; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces weeds and protects roots from heat. Compost feeds the tree and improves soil structure.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for mulch, 2 marks for compost.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: It saves water, it can be made cheaply from a container, and children do not touch the container with dirty hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for the home.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is thrown away and replaced, not washed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for throwing, 1 mark for replacing.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
